text.p: HighwayMaster Communications Inc is on target to reach profitability by the end of 1998 and this year will double the installations for its mobile communications network, said chief executive William Saunders.
"We feel comfortable that we should be on target," Saunders told Reuters in an interview. "And we'll have twice as many installations as last year."
The $30 million-a-year company, which provides voice and data transmissions for trucking companies, installed a net total of 5,603 units onto its network last year.
In the latest quarter, the company realized its first positive gross product margin, which rose from negative 12 percent in the fourth quarter to positive 14.3 percent.

Service margin, which was 28.7 in the latest quarter, should rise as the company completes moving its customers off a switching service provided by AT&T Corp and onto a new switching service built by HighwayMaster, Saunders said.
The company is building a second switching center in 1997 and has plans for a third in 1998 in preparation for AutoLink, a mobile communications network the company is developing for passenger cars.
Saunders said HighwayMaster will spend $6 million this year on AutoLink, which he said is targeted for release by 1998.
Motorola Inc and Prince, a subsidiary of Johnson Controls Inc, are working with HighwayMaster on the AutoLink device, which is expected to retail for about $500 plus subscription fees.

"I think they're going to do well on the trucking side, but I believe this AutoLink opportunity is much larger," said Kenneth Toudouze, a technical analyst with Principal Financial Securities Inc in Dallas.
"I'm looking for an automobile manufacturer to step up and say they want to buy AutoLink for their cars."
Toudouze said he continues to rate HighwayMaster as a buy.
